To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of a Bacillus pumilis gene for the secreted metalloendopep-tidase belonging to adamalysin/ reprolysin family is controlled by mechanisms for catabolite and nitrogen catabolic repressions.

The expression of the metaloendopeptidases from Bacillus pumilis is regulated by the TnrA regulator, which is a transcription factor that is involved in the control of the nitrogen metabolism of the cell.

the expression of metalloendopepsidase gene is regulated by carbon and nitrogen catarbolite repression, and that the control of gene expression is carried out via TnrA protein, which is a regulator of nitrogen metabolism, interacting with ammonium transporter proteins GlnK and/or AmtB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first description of the regulation of gene expression of a secreted adamalysin/repolyisin family member.
the identification of regulatory mechanisms of metalloendopeptides expression in B. pumilus.
the first description of the regulation of expression of the gene encoding a member of the adamalysins/reprolysins family of proteases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of Bacillus metalloendopep tase gene is regulated by the TnrA transcriptional regulator in response to the nitrogen status and the CcpA transcription factor in response to carbon catabolite.
the metalloendopetidase of the adamalysins/reprolysin superfamily is controlled by a complex regulatory network involving the catabolite repressors and the nitrogen metabolism regulatory proteins.
the gene expression of the metallopeptidase is controlled by a complex mechanism involving both catabolite regulation and nitrogen metabolism regulatory protein TnrA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of this gene is controlled by two mechanisms, one of which is mediated by the TnrA regulator and the other is a mechanism of carbon and nitrogen repression.
the expression of Bacillus metalloendopep-tidase gene is regulated by the nitrogen and carbon catabolic pathways.

the expression of Bacillus metalloendopep- tase genes is regulated at the transcription level by a complex system of regulatory mechanisms, including the control by nitrogen catabolites and the participation of the TnrA regulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under nitrogen limitation, the expression of the gene for metalloendopep- tidase of B. pumilus is regulated via the nitrogen metabolism regulatory system.
the metalloendopetidase gene is under the control of the nitrogen metabolism regulatory protein GlnK, which is involved in the regulation of the nitrogen metabolism of the cell.
the expression of a gene encoding a metalloendopepsidase of B. pumilus is regulated by mechanisms of carbon (catabolite) and nitrogen (ntr) catabolite regulation, as well as the GlnK/AmtB complex.
